title: TemplarOS application provenance
description: Where one installed copy of an application came from. Mirrors templar_types::variant::AppProvenance, carried on AppManifest.provenance and returned as the provenance_json column of AppIdentity1.ListVariants. Every field is optional on read: a manifest written before provenance existed still parses, and an origin that cannot be determined is Unknown rather than a guess.

origin.description: Which kind of place this copy came from. Not a taxonomy of vendors — a taxonomy of who can write the file.

trust.description: Derived from the origin, never declared by the application. System means the copy is owned by something with administrative rights over the machine (a package, a system manifest, a Flatpak installation); User means a file the person's own account can rewrite at will. Only a System variant may take an exclusive provider role.

source_path.description: The .desktop file or manifest this variant was derived from, absolute.

package_ref.description: The packaging system's own name for this copy: a Debian package name, a Flatpak application ref. Empty when nothing owns it.

version.description: The version the origin reports, verbatim. Displayed, never compared.

desktop_entry_id.description: The merged desktop-entry id this copy exports, e.g. firefox.desktop. Two variants sharing one is strong evidence they are the same application.

launch.description: How the copy is started. Direct is an executable; FlatpakExport is one of Flatpak's export wrappers; Wrapper is a script that starts something else.

executable.description: The resolved executable, absolute. Evidence for grouping; never a root of trust.

sandboxed.description: Whether the copy runs inside a sandbox the system did not build (Flatpak's). Reported so a person can see it, not acted on here.

update_owner.description: Who is expected to update this copy — which is the honest answer to 'why is my browser still old'.

declared_privileges.description: What the copy's own metadata claims it needs. Inert provenance: a claim is a thing to display and to compare against grants, never a grant.

provider_claims.description: Exclusive roles the copy's metadata says it can fill. Also inert: Providers1 decides, and it checks trust first.

logical.description: The logical application this copy belongs to, when the copy's own metadata declares one (a native manifest's logical_app). Grouping otherwise comes from evidence, not from a claim.

first_seen_ms.description: Unix milliseconds when this variant was first recorded. Stable across re-scans; it is what makes 'the older copy' a meaningful phrase.
